summary: This special election filled the Senate seat left open when Marco Rubio resigned. Ashley Moody (Republican), who was appointed to the seat, won over Angie Nixon (Democrat) and Neil Gillespie (independent).

candidates.name: Ashley Moody
candidates.bio: Republican U.S. senator from Florida, appointed by Gov. Ron DeSantis and sworn in January 21, 2025 after Marco Rubio became secretary of state. She served as Florida attorney general from 2019 to 2025 and as a circuit judge in Hillsborough County from 2006. She is a University of Florida graduate and sits on the Judiciary, HELP and Aging committees, among others.

positions.summary: Supports "No Tax on Tips," "No Tax on Overtime" and "No Tax on Social Security" policies, according to local public radio.
Has introduced legislation to expand expedited removal for certain immigrants convicted of crimes.
Said at an August 2025 news conference that she has long been an advocate for school choice.
As attorney general, filed a 2023 lawsuit against a federal rule requiring states to set targets to reduce CO2 emissions from road travel.
Cosponsored the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act, according to an October 2025 release from her Senate office.

candidates.name: Angie Nixon
candidates.bio: Democrat first elected to the Florida House of Representatives in 2020, representing Jacksonville, where she was born and raised. She is a union organizer, has led Florida for All, a statewide coalition that registers voters, and runs a bookstore and community hub in Jacksonville. She won the Democratic primary with 56% of the vote, defeating Alex Vindman.

positions.summary: Says she wants lower costs and higher wages and a government that stands up to corporate greed.
Supports Medicare for All and describes health care as a right, not a privilege tied to a paycheck.
Said in 2023 that school choice programs defund public schools.
Supports secure borders with clear and compassionate pathways to citizenship, and her website calls for abolishing ICE and rebuilding immigration enforcement, according to PolitiFact.
Voted against Florida's six-week abortion ban (SB 300) in April 2023.
Has said there needs to be a moratorium on data centers until more research is done.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35). Shares checked on November 25, 2026 against The Green Papers (8,281,789 votes in total), which does not say the count is certified.
